name: spectrum
spectralRadius_pow_le'
result.signature: [Nontrivial A] (a : A) (n : ℕ) : (spectralRadius 𝕜 a) ^ n ≤ spectralRadius 𝕜 (a ^ n)
result.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [inst : NormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra 𝕜 A] [Nontrivial A] (a : A)
  (n : ℕ), spectralRadius 𝕜 a ^ n ≤ spectralRadius 𝕜 (a ^ n)
result.value:
:= by
  cases n
  · simp
  · exact spectralRadius_pow_le a _ (by simp)
result.informal_description: For any non-trivial algebra $A$ over a normed field $\mathbb{K}$, element $a \in A$, and natural number $n$, the $n$-th power of the spectral radius of $a$ is less than or equal to the spectral radius of $a^n$. Formally, $(\rho(a))^n \leq \rho(a^n)$, where $\rho(a)$ denotes the spectral radius of $a$.

name: Matrix
nonneg_iff_posSemidef
result.signature: {A : Matrix n n 𝕜} : 0 ≤ A ↔ A.PosSemidef
result.type: ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] {A : Matrix n n 𝕜}, 0 ≤ A ↔ A.PosSemidef
result.informal_name: Non-Negativity of Matrices via Positive Semidefiniteness
result.informal_description: For a square matrix $ A $ over a real closed-like field $ \mathbb{K} $, the inequality $ 0 \leq A $ holds if and only if $ A $ is positive semidefinite.

name: spectrum
spectralRadius_pow_le
result.signature: (a : A) (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) : (spectralRadius 𝕜 a) ^ n ≤ spectralRadius 𝕜 (a ^ n)
result.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [inst : NormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra 𝕜 A] (a : A) (n : ℕ),
  n ≠ 0 → spectralRadius 𝕜 a ^ n ≤ spectralRadius 𝕜 (a ^ n)
result.value:
:= by
  simp only [spectralRadius, ENNReal.iSup₂_pow_of_ne_zero _ hn]
  refine iSup₂_le fun x hx ↦ ?_
  apply le_iSup₂_of_le (x ^ n) (spectrum.pow_mem_pow a n hx)
  simp
result.informal_description: For any element $a$ in an algebra $A$ over a normed field $𝕜$, and for any positive integer $n$, the $n$th power of the spectral radius of $a$ is less than or equal to the spectral radius of $a^n$. Symbolically, $(\rho(a))^n \leq \rho(a^n)$.

name: Matrix
IsPrimitive
mk
result.signature:
∀ {n : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [inst_2 : Fintype n] [inst_3 : DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n R}, (∀ (i j : n), 0 ≤ A i j) → (∃ k > 0, ∀ (i j : n), 0 < (A ^ k) i j) → A.IsPrimitive
result.type:
∀ {n : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Ring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder R] [inst_2 : Fintype n] [inst_3 : DecidableEq n]
  {A : Matrix n n R}, (∀ (i j : n), 0 ≤ A i j) → (∃ k > 0, ∀ (i j : n), 0 < (A ^ k) i j) → A.IsPrimitive
result.informal_description: Given a square matrix $ A $ over a linearly ordered ring $ R $ with finite index set $ n $, if all entries of $ A $ are non-negative and there exists a positive integer $ k $ such that every entry of $ A^k $ is positive, then $ A $ is primitive.
